findings.reason: Operations.js:307 defines __iterator as an arrow inside the plain function reverseFactory, and line 320 now reads this.size in the reverse && !useKeys branch. The diff removes the reversedSequence.size read along with the comment warning about exactly this. Unlike __iterate at line 298, which uses `function`, this throws when the branch runs.
findings.claim: Reverse iteration of an indexed reversed sequence via __iterator reads this.size inside an arrow function, where this is undefined, so it throws a TypeError.
findings.evidence: `reversedSequence.__iterator = (type, reverse) => { ... useKeys ? entry[0] : reverse ? this.size - ++i : i++ ... }` is an arrow function defined inside the plain function `reverseFactory`. Its callers call it unbound (`reverseFactory(this, false)` at src/CollectionImpl.js:573, `reverseFactory(this, true)` at src/CollectionImpl.js:259 and src/Operations.js:61). In this ES module (strict mode), `this` inside the arrow is therefore `undefined`, and the `reverse && !useKeys` branch throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. The diff deletes the line that read `reversedSequence.size` explicitly, along with its comment explaining this exact problem ("`__iterator` is an arrow function, so `this` is not the reversed sequence here"). The neighbouring `__iterate` at line 298 is declared with `function`, which is why `this.size` works there but not here.

findings.reason: The claim that only ObjectSeq.ts:35 uses reverse is wrong: ArraySeq.ts:37-39, KeyedSeq.ts:122 and slice.ts also chain reverse twice. Those tests appear to go through __iterate/toArray rather than __iterator(reverse=true), but the code alone doesn't settle whether any locked test reaches line 320. This is a coverage concern rather than a defect, so I lowered the severity to low.
findings.claim: No locked test exercises the reversed sequence's __iterator with reverse=true, so the suite may not catch the regression.
findings.evidence: In `__tests__`, a search finds only `i.reverse().reverse().toArray()` (`__tests__/ObjectSeq.ts:35`). `reverse()` on a reversed sequence returns the original collection (`reversedSequence.reverse = () => collection`), so that test never calls the reversed sequence's `__iterator` with `reverse=true`. acceptance.md says only that the baseline tests are locked and gives no fail-to-pass or pass-to-pass test for this branch.
